commit_message:
[Merged] dtls: buffer early CCS to handle UDP reorder

Cache early-arriving CCS in dtls1_state_st and replay it when the
handshake reaches the expected state. Clear the flag in
dtls1_clear_received_buffer().

Add dtls_ccs_reorder_test covering client/server reorder, resumption and mutual TLS.

Reviewed-by: Matt Caswell <matt@openssl.foundation>

fix_commit_message:
Fix a Use-After-Free bug in the DTLS code

The newly added #30225 introduced a UAF bug in the master branch found
by the dtlsserver fuzzer. If a CCS arrives early and there is trailing
data left in the current record at the point that we change epoch then
the buffer holding the trailing data is freed as part of setting up the
new record layer, but we still have dangling references into that buffer
causing the UAF.

Fixes #30487

Reviewed-by: Frederik Wedel-Heinen <fwh.openssl@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Paul Dale <paul.dale@oracle.com>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.foundation>
MergeDate: Fri Apr  3 15:06:50 2026
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/30503)
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix f3dbf6aa79c3 on top of intro 0152e4f9f750 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): The CCS buffering mechanism for UDP reorder tolerance does not account for trailing data in the current record buffer. When an early-arriving CCS is buffered using `has_change_cipher_spec = 1` and `goto redo`, the code continues processing. Later, when the buffered CCS is delivered (when `dtls_ccs_expected()` returns true), it triggers `tls_process_change_cipher_spec()` -> `ssl3_do_change_cipher_spec()` -> `tls1_change_cipher_state()` -> `ssl_set_new_record_layer()`, which frees the old record layer buffer via `dtls_free()` -> `tls_free()` -> `tls_int_free()` -> `ossl_tls_buffer_release()`. However, if there is trailing data left in the current record at the point of the cipher change, the pointers to that buffer become dangling. Subsequent reads via `dtls1_read_bytes()` access freed memory, causing a heap-use-after-free. Root cause: The CCS buffering mechanism using `has_change_cipher_spec = 1` and `goto redo` does not verify that all data in the current record buffer has been consumed before allowing a cipher state change. When the buffered CCS triggers ssl_set_new_record_layer(), the old buffer is freed, but dangling pointers to trailing data in that buffer remain, leading to use-after-free on subsequent reads.
